# tests/fixtures

Hand-checked inputs that tests and the evaluation set read. Nothing here is generated by a run.

## target_questions_northwind.md

The gold standard question set the AI prompt is tuned against: the worked ten-question set from
**section 6 of docs/RESEARCH_BOARD_PACKS.md**, for a company at 97% NRR and 11 months runway, which
is Northwind (NRR 97.1%, runway 11.0 mo, Q2 2026). Five themes, ten questions, each with its
provenance marker and a source line naming where it came from.

It is copied from section 6, not written here. tests/test_score_questions.py compares it to the
document word for word, so an edit to either one that leaves them apart fails a test. The one
deliberate difference is question 3's scoping clause, and the file's own header lists it.

### Format

    # Target question set: Northwind

    Company profile: ...
    Source: docs/RESEARCH_BOARD_PACKS.md, section 6.

    ## Theme: Retention decomposition

    1. [verbatim with values] Question text.
       Source: where it came from.

    2. [constructed] Question text.
       Source: where it came from.

Rules the parser enforces, so a mistake stops rather than scores:

- Every question sits under a `## Theme: name` heading. Themes may hold any number of questions.
- Every question is a numbered line carrying exactly one provenance marker in square brackets.
- The only markers allowed are `verbatim`, `verbatim with values` and `constructed`. Anything else
  stops the run and names the line.
- Any line that is not a theme heading or a numbered question is ignored, which is how the header
  and the indented source lines can hold notes. A test checks that every question has its source line.

### What the markers mean

These are section 6's own definitions of its three marks:

- `verbatim` (section 6's **[V]**): verbatim from the cited source.
- `verbatim with values` (**[V+]**): a verbatim question or instruction with the company's values
  inserted.
- `constructed` (**[C]**): constructed by that report on a sourced finding, quotable to no one.

Two of section 6's rows carry two marks, and a question here carries one. Question 3 keeps the
table's `[V]` (its scoping clause is constructed); question 10 is a constructed first clause plus a
verbatim second clause with no lead named, so it takes the weaker mark, `constructed`. The source
line under each says which part is which.

The mix matters when reading a score. A generated set that reaches a theme only through questions
the target marked `constructed` is weaker evidence than one that lands on the sourced questions,
which is why the 1 to 5 rubric asks about it.

### What the target does not score

The target does not pass the scorer's own checks at 100%: 5 of 10 on decomposition and 6 of 10 on
naming a metric and a value (the fixture's header says which questions and why). The scorecard
prints those two rates beside every set's, so a set is read against the standard.

### Scoring against it

    python eval/score_questions.py output/northwind_analysis.json
    python eval/score_questions.py my_questions.md --target tests/fixtures/target_questions_northwind.md
    python eval/score_questions.py --rubric
